item.title: Waiting for the Call: A Journey of Resilience Through Chronic Illness
item.description: Marquita Sams, a professional dancer diagnosed with Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) at 17, has used her experiences to found a nonprofit to raise awareness about organ donation, transition into a new career as a therapist and social worker, and publish an e-book to help others facing chronic illness. The post Waiting for the Call: A Journey of Resilience Through Chronic Illness appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Washington Gas Celebrates Black History Month
item.description: Tamara Neal, Director and Senior Station Leader at Washington Gas, reflects on her journey from the below-ground crew truck to her current role, and how Black History Month is a time to celebrate the strength, courage, and brilliance of those who came before us. The post Washington Gas Celebrates Black History Month appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Advocates to D.C. Council: We Need New Leaders at PSC for Lower Ratepayer Bills, Not More Utility Handouts
item.description: A coalition of consumer, housing and climate advocates is urging the D.C. Council to pause new appointments to the Public Service Commission until after the new mayor takes office, citing the commission's repeated failures to keep energy bills down and its bias towards for-profit utility corporations. The post Advocates to D.C. Council: We Need New Leaders at PSC for Lower Ratepayer Bills, Not More Utility Handouts appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Industrial Bank to Advance Communities with $75 Million in New Market Tax Credits
item.description: Industrial Bank has been awarded a $75 million New Markets Tax Credit allocation to promote community impact efforts for low-income populations across the DMV, providing flexible lending terms and investing in critical services and infrastructure. The post Industrial Bank to Advance Communities with $75 Million in New Market Tax Credits appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Rail Merger Aims to Enhance Quality of Life
item.description: A proposed merger between two major rail carriers could reduce truck traffic, improve air quality, and lower transportation costs for families, while also benefiting workers and local economies. The post Rail Merger Aims to Enhance Quality of Life appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: In Ward 1 D.C. Council Race, the Fight Continues for Affordability and Responsive Government
item.description: Five candidates are running for the Ward 1 seat on the D.C. Council, with Trindade Deramo focusing on housing affordability, public safety, community concerns, and transportation connectivity, while preserving the legacy of U Street as Black Broadway. The post In Ward 1 D.C. Council Race, the Fight Continues for Affordability and Responsive Government appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: D.C. Students Kick Off 44th Annual Spelling Bee Season
item.description: Over 260 students from 88 schools in Washington, D.C., competed in the annual Citywide Spelling Bee, with the goal of qualifying for the Scripps National Spelling Bee in May, while the focus was on building skills and learning life lessons. The post D.C. Students Kick Off 44th Annual Spelling Bee Season appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: DMV Native Myles Frost Stars in ‘Chez Joey’ at Arena Stage
item.description: Myles Frost, the youngest solo actor to win a Tony Award, is starring in Arena Stage's "Chez Joey," a reimagined musical inspired by John O'Hara's "Pal Joey," co-directed by Savion Glover and Tony Goldwyn, featuring new tunes and arrangements, and an outstanding cast. The post DMV Native Myles Frost Stars in ‘Chez Joey’ at Arena Stage appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.description: Rev. Jesse L. item.title: Rev. Graylan Scott Hagler, D.C. Pastor, Activist and Prophetic Voice for Justice, Dies
item.description: Rev. Graylan Scott Hagler, a longtime Washington, D.C., pastor and social justice advocate, died Tuesday after a battle with cancer, leaving behind a legacy of faith-rooted activism and community leadership.
